title: CommandResult
description: The single JSON document a loxicmd invocation writes to stdout under -o json. Exactly one document per invocation; progress and prose go to stderr. Every key listed here is always present: an empty value is emitted as "", {} or [] and never as null. Secret material is prohibited from every field, including data and warnings; secret-bearing keys are omitted entirely rather than masked.

apiVersion.description: Envelope contract version. A breaking envelope change requires a new value here; consumers reject an unknown major.

command.description: Dotted command path that produced this result, e.g. "get.snapshot", "appliance.status".

success.description: True exactly when the process exit code is 0.

code.description: Machine verdict, in one-to-one correspondence with the exit-code taxonomy (see exit-codes.md): OK=0, INVALID_ARGUMENT=2, AUTH=3, PRECONDITION=4, UNAVAILABLE=5, CONTRACT_MISMATCH=6, FAILED=7, PARTIAL=8.

message.description: Human-readable summary of the verdict. Empty on success. Never contains secret material.

correlationId.description: Identifier correlating this invocation across the CLI, the gateway or backend it called, and their logs/journals. Empty only when no downstream call was attempted.

data.description: Command-specific payload. Its schema is versioned per command. On failure it preserves the error origin without loss: data.origin ("cli"|"gateway"|"oam"|"backend"|"os"), data.httpStatus (integer, 0 when no HTTP exchange happened), and data.componentCode (the downstream component's own error code, verbatim) are present on every failure so automation never parses message strings.

operationId.description: Present when the command started or observed a long-running or partially applied operation; used to query progress or drive recovery.

warnings.description: Conditions that did not change the verdict but that an operator or automation should see. Machine-readable; prose-only progress goes to stderr instead.
